question: Price makes a higher high at the end of the chart while RSI makes a lower high. What is this called and how should it be used?
options: Bearish (negative) divergence; a warning of fading momentum that needs price confirmation, such as a break of support
A hidden bullish divergence that favours adding to long positions
Bullish (positive) divergence; momentum is confirming the new high
Positive reversal; it signals the uptrend will accelerate

question: At point A the 10-period rate of change crosses above its zero line. What does this tell you?
options: Price has just crossed above its 10-period moving average, confirming that a new uptrend is under way
ROC has reached an overbought level, so a pullback is likely
The close is now above the close of 10 periods earlier: momentum has turned positive
Price has risen 10% from its low

question: Up-trendlines are drawn on both price and its 10-bar momentum. What is the best interpretation of the sequence shown?
options: Price broke its trendline first and momentum then confirmed, which is the normal sequence
The momentum break was an early warning that the advance was losing force; the later break of the price trendline confirmed it
Because momentum was still above zero when its trendline broke, the break signalled bullish continuation
The momentum break is a complete sell signal on its own, so the price trendline break adds no information

question: After a long decline, RSI surges to the extreme reading at M within weeks of the low. How is such a 'mega-overbought' reading best interpreted?
options: As a sign of exceptional upside momentum typical of the early stage of a new advance; the first pullback is more likely to be a buying opportunity than the final top
As a reliable sell signal, because a reading this far above 70 normally marks an intermediate top in a bear-market rally
As a bearish divergence, because RSI has risen faster than price
As evidence that the rally is exhausted and the prior decline will resume

options: -8.89%; the long-term average is above the short-term average, a bearish reading
+8.16%; the short-term average is above the long-term average, upside momentum
+8.89%; the gap is bearish because the short-term average has crossed the long-term average from above
+8.89%; the short-term average is above the long-term average, upside momentum
